subject.title: [Bug]: Slack Socket Mode ghost connections after gateway restart silently drop inbound messages

question: Should direct Slack Socket Mode stay warning-only for multiple active connections, or should OpenClaw add automatic restart-ghost recovery/fencing after live proof?
rationale: Slack documents multiple active Socket Mode connections as valid, but this report shows a single-gateway restart path where old connections can silently steal events; automation cannot choose the compatibility and false-positive policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Live-proof targeted recovery
options.body: Require a real Slack restart reproduction, then implement plugin-owned recovery that targets stale same-gateway ghosts without breaking intentional multi-gateway, relay, or HTTP deployments.

options.title: Keep warning-only behavior
options.body: Treat the current diagnostic plus relay/HTTP guidance as the supported policy and leave the stop-wait-start workaround for direct Socket Mode restarts.

options.title: Prefer relay or HTTP for production
options.body: Document direct Socket Mode as single-gateway best effort and steer production multi-gateway or restart-sensitive deployments to relay mode or HTTP Request URLs.

recommendation.title: Live-proof targeted recovery
recommendation.body: Require a real Slack restart reproduction, then implement plugin-owned recovery that targets stale same-gateway ghosts without breaking intentional multi-gateway, relay, or HTTP deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history shows the broadest recent ownership across Slack provider lifecycle, gateway health policy, and channel reliability decisions.
